**Market Parameters Report – June 2009** 





### **1. Demand for platinum** 

- _We have lowered our demand estimates for platinum, sharply so in 2009, as the effects of the slump in auto production together with reduced capital spending glass, petroleum refining and chemicals production become increasingly apparent.  This is cushion to a degree by increased estimates for retail investment where we see the generally moderate price environment as conducive to higher net inflows._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|3,814|3,019|3,220|3,596|
|Jewellery|1,646|1,968|2,095|2,263|
|_Chemical_|346|307|303|389|
|_Electronics_|378|320|326|343|
|_Glass_|444|123|352|412|
|_Petroleum_|200|225|298|242|
|_Retail investment_|452|390|195|115|
|_Other_|461|426|459|510|
|Industrial|2,281|1,791|1,932|2,011|
|**Total**|**7,742**|**6,778**|**7,247**|**7,869**|



### **1.1  Autocatalyst** 

- Our estimates for autocatalyst demand now assume a 16% decline in global light vehicle production in 2009 with improvements of 10% and 11% in 2010 and 2011 respectively.  As before, the bulk of the damage in 2009 is in the developed economies of North America, Europe and Japan.  Furthermore, production of heavy duty vehicles in these markets is now expected to fall by 40% this year. 

- Although platinum is benefiting from increased DPF fitment (especially in Europe ahead of Euro 5 regulations from September 2009), it faces continuing headwinds from substitution in gasoline and most notably nowadays in diesel applications where the use of bi‐metallic platinum/palladium catalysts is increasing.  The effects of this are unlikely to be overcome by increases in diesel’s market share, which we expect to remain static at around 25

% of global light vehicle production over the forecast period. 

### **1.2 Jewellery** (reported as gross fabrication) 

- We have assumed that prices will remain supportive for platinum jewellery demand (especially in China) and have made only minor alterations to our forecast.  Our contacts in China have indicated over recent weeks that $1,200 is a critical level for platinum prices, the view being that elevated demand is not sustainable at prices appreciably above this mark. 

### **1.3 Industrial & other applications** 

- Demand for platinum in glass applications is now expected to fall sharply in 2009, reflecting a dramatic curtailment of capacity expansions in LCD glass.  However, panel production has improved considerably over recent weeks, raising fears of a glass shortage later this year and signalling a likely return to capacity expansions in 2010.  Expansions in the chemicals sector have been similarly affected in 2009 but less dramatically.  Meanwhile, estimates for retail investment demand have been scaled up.

### **2. Demand for palladium** 

- _Our forecast of total palladium demand in 2009 has been reduced due to weaker autocatalyst consumption.  However, demand in 2010 and 2011 is aided by substitution gains in diesel and gasoline as well as recovering vehicle production.  With little change in other applications, our estimates for overall demand in these two years are little changed._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|4,408|3,708|4,351|4,865|
|Jewellery|1,301|1,352|1,452|1,535|
|_Dental_|776|742|730|717|
|_Chemical_|385|279|317|375|
|_Electronics_|1,347|1,186|1,304|1,461|
|_Retail investment_|84|170|85|58|
|_Other_|91|76|86|93|
|Industrial|2,683|2,453|2,522|2,703|
|**Total**|**8,391**|**7,512**|**8,326**|**9,102**|



### **2.1 Autocatalyst** 

- As with platinum, our forecast for palladium demand in autocatalyst has suffered from scaled back auto production estimates.  This is particularly evident in 2009, following which we expect palladium to recover more strongly than platinum due to the positive effects of substitution and improvements in emerging market vehicle production; mainly gasoline. 

### **2.2 Jewellery** (reported as gross fabrication) 

- Our forecasts for jewellery fabrication are largely unchanged.  Although the price environment may suggest stronger demand, palladium’s progress has been slowed by the relative affordability of platinum jewellery versus prices over the last two years and crucially, versus gold.  Platinum remains the aspirational choice in the key Chinese market and is now perceived as competitively priced.  Meanwhile, palladium continues to lack the marketing budget of platinum and gold jewellery, the effect of which is now all too obvious. 

### **2.3 Industrial** 

- In overall terms, our forecasts in this area have been raised fractionally.  We are more positive rega

rding dental and retail investment demand (the latter in 2009) and these are offsetting a significant decline in the chemicals sector where capital spending in 2009 has been cut severely.

### **3. Supply** 

### **3.1  Platinum supply** 

- _Our forecast of total platinum supply in 2009 has been scaled back due to a downgrade in autocatalyst recovery volumes.  We expect supply from this source to resume its growth from 2010.  Otherwise, our forecast of mine production is largely unchanged and with some increases in jewellery scrap, our forecast of overall platinum supply in 2010 and 2011 is little changed from our previous estimates._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|4,671|4,655|4,920|5,237|
|Russia|835|799|792|786|
|Canada|227|201|268|276|
|United States|115|107|92|80|
|Zimbabwe|180|195|222|240|
|Others|123|112|109|109|
|**Total mineproduction**|**6,151**|**6,069**|**6,403**|**6,729**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|998|883|1,075|1,174|
|Jewelleryscrap|910|299|281|264|
|**Total supply**|**8,059**|**7,250**|**7,759**|**8,167**|



- We remain of the view that platinum mine production in South Africa will stabilise in 2009 with a likely re‐emergence of growth from 2010.  New mines entering production this year should be sufficient to offset lower output from established operations and the exceptional events of 2008 are not expected to recur.  However, risk to the downside remains, with the strengthening of the rand since March having offset improved USD platinum prices. 

- The collapse of PGM and steel prices in the second half of 2008 caused a marked slow‐down in the flow of autocatalyst scrap for recycling.  This continued into the early months of 2009 and has been aggravated by the reduced scrapping of old vehicles as the slump in new vehicle sales developed.  We have therefore marked down our forecasts of platinum recovery, especially in 2009.  Autocatalyst scrap flows have improved in recent weeks and in theory should be boosted by the effect of scrappage programmes in some European markets.  However, these schemes require the retired vehicles to be scrapped domestically rather than exported for re‐use in other countries.  This is likely to choke the recycling infrastructure in some European countries, thus postponing some of this flow into 2010. 

- We have raised our forecasts of jewellery scrap recycling.  Even though prices are unlikely to trigger outflows on the scale of 2008, the recycling infrastructure in the key Japanese market has grown in sophistication and coverage and is expected to capture significant volumes going forward, despite moderate platinum prices.

### **3.2  Palladium supply** 

- _With reduced estimates for autocatalyst recycling, palladium supply is expected to fall sharply in 2009 but recovery strongly in 2011 an

d again in 2011 (note: this excludes supply from state owned stocks in Russia)._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|2,366|2,533|2,730|2,955|
|Russia|2,712|2,600|2,600|2,600|
|Canada|524|297|369|373|
|United States|384|354|304|268|
|Zimbabwe|140|152|176|191|
|Others|255|250|245|245|
|**Total mineproduction**|**6,381**|**6,186**|**6,425**|**6,633**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|1,184|1,068|1,407|1,743|
|Jewelleryscrap|195|138|146|162|
|**Total supply**|**7,759**|**7,392**|**7,978**|**8,538**|



- In downgrading our view of autocatalyst recycling, this has had a more significant impact on palladium recovery, which we now see as substantially lower in 2009 than previously forecast.  With little change in our view of mine production, this produces a sharp fall in overall palladium supply in 2009, followed by a strong recovery from 2010 driven by improved mine production and higher recycling volumes. 

- After a downturn this year, growth in autocatalyst recycling should resume from 2010, driving palladium recovery to an eventual peak of around 2m ounces by 2012; double the level we are now forecasting for 2009.

### **4. Market balances** 

### **4.1 Platinum** 

- _We estimate that platinum will register a recurring gross surplus over each of the forecast years.  This will be especially large in 2009 and 2010.  Consequently, both above‐ground stocks and net investment in platinum will rise over the forecast period._ 

- _We have raised our estimates for net investment in ETFs over all the forecast years but remain of the view that net inflows are likely to weaken from 2010.  This excludes the possibility of a US listed ETF as this remains undecided._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|New supply|8,059|7,250|7,759|8,167|
|Fabrication demand|7,742|6,778|7,247|7,869|
|**_Gross surplus(deficit)_**|**317**|**472**|**513**|**297**|
|ETF demand|(102)|(250)|(160)|(120)|
|**Residual surplus(deficit)**|**215**|**222**|**353**|**177**|



### **4.2 Palladium** 

- _We now see palladium in gross deficit in each of the forecast years, although this is expected to be quite slender in 2009.  On the whole, this is due to reduced supply estimated, although demand in 2009 has also been scaled back._ 

- _Our forecasts for Russian stock sales and net ETF inflows have both been increased. However, this produces a similar profile at the residual level to our previous estimates.  This suggests that the overall market for palladium will be close to balance by 2011, assuming that Russian stock sales ease from 2010._

### **5. Above‐ground stocks** 

- _Above‐ground stocks are implied from historical trade data for Switzerland (dating from 1970) and declared stocks on the Nymex and Tocom futures exchanges.  Excluded are stocks held by governments (including Russia), producers, refiners and fabricators and consumers._ 

|**Implied stocks**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Platinum:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|1.86|2.33|2.84|3.14|
|Demand cover(months)|2.9|4.1|4.7|4.8|
|**Palladium:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|7.67|8.85|9.30|9.39|
|Demand cover(months)|11.0|14.1|13.4|12.4|



- Over the next three years platinum’s demand cover is expected to rise from around three months to approaching five months as its gross surplus persists. 

- For palladium, above‐ground stocks are forecast to remain substantial over the forecast period at more than one year’s demand cover.  Although recurring gross deficits create downward pressure, this will be more than offset by continuing inflows of palladium from Russian state stocks into Swiss vaults. 

- _Note: forecast sales of palladium from Russian state stocks have now been included as inflows to implied above‐ground stocks in Switzerland.  These inclusions serve to inflate stocks in Switzerland but are balanced by commensurate declines in Russia’s state owned inventories._

### **6. Prices and related indicators** 

### **6.1 Platinum** 

_Platinum encounters strong resistance on the approach to $1,300 on dollar strength and weakness in gold.  Currently trading in the $1,165 area. Volatility jumped on platinum’s abrupt retreat to $1,200._ 



_Technically motivated traders will have seen the RSI approaching 70 as a clear sell signal and a time for profit taking.  They would, of course, have been right._ 



_Platinum has now dipped below the 50 day moving average. This is not overly supportive and suggests the likelihood of further easing to around the $1,100 level._ 



Page | 7 

**Market Parameters Report – June 2009** 





### **6.2 Palladium** 

_Palladium has been tracking platinum for the most part but has been more resilient in this week’s general sell‐off. However, if platinum weakens further, this is unlikely to be sustained._ 

_Palladium’s RSI pattern almost identical to platinum and will have been a sell signal at prices near $250._ 

_Palladium looks near identical to platinum, with spot having fallen through the 50 day average; not a good sign and is much more suggestive of $200 than $250._
